question: Short stature is defined as a height-for-age below −2 SD from the mean for age and sex on WHO or IAP growth charts; a height below −3 SD is classified as severe short stature.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Short stature is height-for-age < −2 SD; severe short stature is < −3 SD, as defined on the WHO 2006 growth standards and IAP charts used in India. Ensure you can recall these thresholds precisely, as they determine when investigations and referral are warranted.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The −2 SD threshold defines short stature and the −3 SD threshold defines severe short stature on WHO/IAP charts. These cut-offs are the starting point for all clinical and investigative decisions in a child presenting with possible growth failure.
